title: INT-05 · Disinformation: language signals and verification

blocks.text: INT-05 · Disinformation: language signals and verification
Lesson overview

In the Arab information ecosystem, false, misleading or deleted content circulates daily alongside news: messages sent in family groups, old photos presented as new, invented quotes, sites that mimic real newspapers. There is also an Arab journalistic genre dedicated to verification ( ⁧تَدْقِيقُ المَعْلُومَاتِ⁩ ), with a vocabulary and its own structure. In this unit learn the types of misinformation and their Arabic names, language signals that make a content suspicious, verification steps as they are described by fact-checking platforms, and the vocabulary of the verification articles ( ⁧الاِدِّعَاء⁩ , ⁧التَّقْيِيم⁩ , ⁧مُضَلِّل⁩ , ⁧خَارِجَ سِيَاقِهِ⁩ ). The method is the public one of media education: no operational technique. Two weeks.

rows: B2-08 → B2-12; INT-04; EGY-12 (news and voices)
12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 205–206), plus the ARZ/EGY track

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Arab news verification platforms (Appendix C), session with the tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. appoint and distinguish the main types of misinformation in Arabic;
2. recognizing the linguistic signals of a suspicious content (urgency, emotion, vague sources, appeals to
sharing);
3. describe in Arabic the steps of a verification: source, date, author, context, comparison;
4. read an Arabic fact-checking article and report the verdict precisely;
5. write a brief verification of an invented content, with the vocabulary and structure of the genre.
Two-week plan.

blocks.text: ⁧فَوَاتُ الأَوَانِ⁩ Too late. ⁧نِطَاق⁩ "Radio, ampo" · ⁧صَادِم⁩ • Shocking · ⁧مُدَوٍّ⁩ ( ⁧مُدَوِّيَة⁩ ) * "Scary" is a song by the American singer-songwriter Jimmy. A signal is not evidence. A text full of exclamation points can be true, and a sober text can be false. The signals tell you how much to verify, not what is true.
4. The steps of verification

rows: Who published it first? It's recognizable, does it have a story?
Is it recent? is connected to an actual event?

blocks.text: 3 · the author ⁧مَنْ كَتَبَهُ أَوْ قَالَهُ؟⁩ Is it real? Is he competent? Did he really say that?

rows: where and when was the content (photo, video, sentence) born?
Do they report reliable and independent sources?
Is it on the institution's website, in the original document?

blocks.text: Images. For images, the verification platforms describe reverse search ( ⁧البَحْثُ العَكْسِيُّ عَنِ الصُّوَرِ⁩ ): search where and when an image first appeared. Many photos of today are old or taken elsewhere ( ⁧خَارِجَ سِيَاقِهَا⁩ ).
